recipe_name: Miso Salmon with Coconut Rice and Charred Broccolini
tags: seafood, impressive, family-favourite, full-meal, weeknight, entertaining, healthy-ish
pairings: Cucumber and spring onion garnish, Sesame seeds, Cold Sapporo or sake
nathan_tweaks: The miso marinade is the whole point — don't skimp on the marinating time. Charred broccolini is the preferred green. This works as a complete dinner; everything is timed to come together at once if you start the rice first.
substitutions: Works with ocean trout or barramundi. Swap broccolini for broccolini or bok choy. Use regular short-grain rice if jasmine isn't available.
ingredients: 4 salmon fillets (approx. 180g each) | 2 tbsp white miso paste | 1 tbsp soy sauce | 1 tbsp honey | 1 tsp sesame oil | 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated (optional) | 1.5 cups jasmine rice | 400ml coconut milk | 1 cup water | 1 tsp salt | 2 bunches broccolini | Olive oil | Salt | Lemon wedges | 1/2 cucumber, thinly sliced (to serve) | 2 spring onions, sliced (to serve) | 1 tbsp sesame seeds (to serve)
method: Mix miso paste, soy sauce, honey and sesame oil together. Add grated ginger if using. Coat salmon fillets and leave to marinate for 15–30 minutes. | Rinse jasmine rice until water runs clear. Combine rice, coconut milk, water and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from heat and leave covered for 5 minutes. | Preheat oven to 200°C. Place marinated salmon on a lined baking tray. Roast for 12–15 minutes depending on thickness — it should be just cooked through with a slightly lacquered top. | While salmon roasts, heat a large heavy pan or griddle until very hot. Toss broccolini with olive oil and salt. Char in the hot pan for 4–5 minutes, turning occasionally, until bright green and blistered in places. | Serve salmon over coconut rice, broccolini alongside, with cucumber and spring onion scattered over the top. Finish with sesame seeds and a lemon wedge.

method: Heat a large heavy-based pan or griddle over high heat until very hot — it should be slightly smoking. | Toss broccolini with olive oil and a good pinch of salt. | Add broccolini to the hot pan in a single layer.
